lines: Russo-Ukrainian war Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war Ukraine launches a large-scale drone attack across western Russia, striking the Perm refinery in Perm Krai and Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov Oblast. (The Kyiv Independent) (The Moscow Times)

Kurdish–Turkish conflict Turkish intelligence reports that the Kurdistan Workers' Party withdraws from 14 additional bases in northern Iraq as part of an ongoing disarmament process aimed at ending its conflict with Turkey. (AFP via France 24)

At least 15 people are injured and 28 houses and shops are vandalised during clashes between rival Bangladesh Nationalist Party factions in Shailkupa Upazila, Jhenaidah District, Bangladesh. (The Daily Star)

At least 20 people are injured, five seriously, and several shops are vandalised as rival factions of the banned Awami League clash and detonate four crude bombs in Gopalganj Sadar Upazila, Gopalganj District, Bangladesh. (The Business Standard)

Jensen Huang scandal, Chinese intelligence activity abroad Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer less than two weeks after he resigned following revelations of an affair with Alice Huang, who is suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for China. (CBS)
Seven people are killed and two others are injured after a truck loaded with stones overturns onto a minitruck in Punjab, Pakistan. (Xinhua)
Tajikistan formally begins the process of withdrawing from the International Criminal Court. (Reuters)

2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis The Supreme Court of Spain grants amnesty to former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont, who is currently in self-imposed exile in Belgium, thereby bringing the legal proceedings against the leaders of the October 2017 declaration of independence to a definitive close. (CNN)
2026 European bomb threat wave Hundreds of schools across Denmark and Germany receive bomb threats via email, with police ordering the schools to continue operations as normal. (Reuters)

2026 European unrest A 58-year-old student dies at Sapienza University in Rome, Italy, while being on a hunger strike protesting the fact that he had not been assigned a place to stay. (Fanpage in Italian)
Hijab in Iran Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi receives 74 lashes for performing at a music concert without a hijab. (BBC)

2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup bids In association football, FIFA confirms Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, and the United States as joint hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales will jointly host the 2035 tournament. (AFP)
